label: Figure 11.1: The demand curves for the industry and the firm in perfect competition
alt: Two graphs: the industry, where downward-sloping demand D and upward-sloping supply S meet at price P and quantity Q; and the firm, whose demand D = AR = MR is a horizontal line at the industry price P.
caption: In the industry graph, supply S and demand D determine the market price P and quantity Q. The individual firm is a price taker: at that price it can sell any quantity it likes, so its demand curve D = AR = MR is a horizontal line at P (note the firm’s quantity axis is on a much smaller scale).
